Please review the following manuscript. I feel positive about this paper. My overall impression is good, and I'd be pleased to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
    print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
from pathlib import Path
print('Local agent instructions:', list(Path('.').glob('AGENTS.md')))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
pdf = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
out = Path('tmp/pdfs')
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES', len(pdf.pages))
texts = []
for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
    text = page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    texts.append('\\n\\n===== PAGE %d =====\\n\\n%s' % (i+1, text))
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

strengths: The reported accuracy gains are substantial. At 50 images per class, WMDD achieves 57.6% on ImageNet-1K versus 53.5% for the strongest listed baseline, and 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet versus 48.7% (Table 1). These results suggest practical value for large-scale image classification.

Combining representative feature targets with per-class BatchNorm regularization provides a straightforward distillation pipeline without bilevel optimization. Table 4 supports the benefit of combining these components.

Evaluation covers several compression budgets and transfer from ResNet-18 to larger ResNets and vision transformers. The feature-layer, regularization, and sliced-Wasserstein experiments provide useful additional evidence.

The main pipeline is clearly presented, with equations, pseudocode, implementation settings, and a code link. Relevant datasets, prior distillation methods, and optimal-transport software are credited. Appendix A appropriately acknowledges that distilled data can inherit source-dataset biases.
weaknesses: The central formulation needs clearer positioning against standard quantization. With one input distribution, squared Euclidean cost, and freely optimized weights, Eq. (5) reduces to the k-means objective: minimizing the average squared distance from each real feature to its nearest prototype. This connection is neither discussed nor tested through a k-means implementation using identical PCBN and relabeling. Consequently, the additional contribution of the transport formulation and solver remains unclear.

The MMD comparison does not adequately isolate the metric. At 1 image per class, the proposed barycenter is the class feature mean, making Eq. (12) identical to linear-MMD mean matching when the encoder is held fixed. Figure 4 nevertheless reports 5.77% versus 0.48%. Removing augmentations and FKD does not resolve the pretrained-versus-random encoder distinction described in Section 5.6. Appendix B supplies generic risk bounds, but does not establish a tighter guarantee explaining WMDD's advantage.

The baseline protocols require reconciliation. On ImageNet-1K at 10 images per class, Table 4's CE-plus-standard-BN configuration achieves 35.9%, whereas Table 1 reports 21.3% for SRe2L. Meanwhile, replacing CE with the Wasserstein objective under PCBN improves 36.4% to 38.1%. The much larger unexplained baseline discrepancy makes it difficult to attribute the headline gains to the proposed components.

The solver description leaves a substantive implementation ambiguity. Algorithm 2 computes a transport plan, updates its target weights, and then reuses the old plan for the position update. That plan retains the old column marginals, so the Hessian relation in Eq. (35) cannot simply use the updated weights. The manuscript should clarify or correct this sequence. Barycenter initialization, the weight-update learning rate, handling of zero weights in Eq. (11), and the precise application of weights during FKD are also insufficiently specified.

Efficiency evidence is narrower than the scalability claim. Table 3 compares methods only on ImageNette at 1 image per class; Table 5 adds Tiny ImageNet timings. An ImageNet-1K comparison separating teacher training, feature extraction, transport computation, image synthesis, and relabeling would better establish the claimed overall computational benefit.
